en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands according to the 2016 NAMRIA count, not the previously taught number of 7,107.
Despite being the tallest mountain, Mount Apo has never had a recorded historical eruption.
The Cagayan River, at approximately 505 kilometers long, is the longest river in the Philippines.
Lake Taal, with a maximum depth of about 172 meters, is the deepest lake in the Philippines.
The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, stretching about 540 kilometers along eastern Luzon.
The Philippines has 24 active volcanoes monitored by PHIVOLCS, not just one or two.
The famous Chocolate Hills geological formation is located in the province of Bohol, not Cebu.
Mount Apo, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level, is the highest mountain in the Philippines.
The Philippine Sea lies to the east of the Philippine archipelago, not to the west.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park sits in the open Sulu Sea, about 150 kilometers from the nearest landmass.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is the only landlocked region in the Philippines, having no coastline along any sea.
The West Philippine Sea is the official Philippine government name for the eastern portion of the South China Sea, not a separate body of water.
